historical_reviews.deepseek: Its literal no-data request silently chooses one side of the source contradiction and therefore is not execution-ready authority.

original_test_intent: Read a verified platform's BMC, BIOS, system-FPGA and HIB-FPGA revision tuple through the Wistron OEM command and compare it with an approved firmware inventory baseline.
original_method: Preserve both source request variants and the stated no-request note. Do not execute until the approved Wistron command contract resolves whether NetFn 0x30 Cmd 0x20 takes an interface-selector byte and confirms the ten-byte response layout.
manual_activity: The platform owner supplies and approves the firmware-scoped Wistron 0x30/0x20 contract, resolves selector/no-request semantics, identifies the target and provides expected component versions.
required_inputs: Verified platform/BMC identity and firmware family
Decision on Ethernet Interface Select presence and allowed values
Approved response length and field encoding
Expected version matrix and formatting rules
safety_requirements: Do not guess or probe selector values
Do not assume in-band and OOB payloads differ without specification
Validate completion and approved response length
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and approved OEM contract
Construct exactly one approved in-band or OOB request
Capture the full redacted request and response
Compare each component with the expected matrix
Archive raw bytes and no-mutation evidence
engineer_actions: Resolve the source request contradiction and approve the contract
Approve component identities and expected versions
Own unknown-field interpretation and final DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's no-data OOB request matches one Procedure branch but contradicts the in-band selector and Request N/A ambiguity; it must not be executed as the authoritative form.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After the Wistron contract is approved, issue exactly one secret-safe raw 0x30 0x20 [approved-interface-selector-if-required] request on the specified path, then decode only the contract-defined BMC/BIOS/system-FPGA/HIB-FPGA bytes.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both source request variants, the Request N/A note, response map and 10/5 timing are preserved pending resolution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Pin the OEM schema to platform and firmware, resolve the request bytes before execution, validate the entire returned structure and compare a named four-component version tuple with an approved matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the source contradiction explicit and prevents one path from silently overriding another.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Standard BMC inventory or a subset of components cannot replace the OEM command's system/HIB FPGA coverage; this read does not authorize firmware updates.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OEM layouts may vary across firmware families, and revision bytes may be packed or formatted differently than simple decimal major/minor values.

project_override_considerations: An alternate Redfish/vendor inventory is equivalent only if it exposes all four named components with a documented one-to-one mapping and canonical version encoding; otherwise OEM coverage remains open.
expected_evidence: Approved vendor contract and target/platform/firmware identity
Redacted full raw request/response and completion
Decoded four-component version tuple plus expected-matrix comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Procedure requires an Ethernet Interface Select byte for the in-band request, omits it for the OOB request, and separately states Request N/A. These are incompatible request schemas for the same OEM command and require an approved Wistron/firmware ruling before execution.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only purpose and affected components are clear. The missing OEM contract and owner resolution are identifiable prerequisites, so the review is REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Stops the unreviewed no-data command from winning by convenience, binds the OEM layout to platform/firmware and turns the response into a named four-component inventory comparison.
independent_technical_reasoning: OEM NetFn 0x30 does not provide portable semantics. An extra selector byte changes the request framing, so the source's with-selector, without-selector and Request N/A forms cannot all be authoritative. Even a successful response cannot be decoded safely unless the platform-specific length and revision encoding are pinned. The correct boundary is therefore a read-only but contract-gated execution, not speculative probing.
